_comment: Hardware: qrb5165_flowc -- QRB5165 v66 through Flow C: HTA (CPU_P) + Hexagon v66 DSP (CPU_E) + Kryo 585 CPU (CPU_X), one lane each. Profiles are the tile-level results.csv files flowc/artifacts.py writes from measurements/qrb5165_v66.json.

Periodic taskset -- each model runs at its OWN period, drawn from the model bank's period_ms and snapped to a multiple of the fastest task's (8 ms) so the hyperperiod is just the slowest period (8 ms):
mlp_control: period 8 ms (125.0 Hz), 1 copy(ies), 0.107 ms each (serial on CPU, 1 dispatches), 1.3% of a core, 3 instances over the horizon
mlp_control: window 5 ms (drawn from window_ms 2-8 ms, then fitted to the period; deadline = 40.83x measured runtime), start_time 0 ms
fused_split: period 8 ms (125.0 Hz), 1 copy(ies), 5.154 ms each (serial on DSP, 3 dispatches), 64.4% of a core, 3 instances over the horizon
fused_split: window 6 ms (drawn from window_ms 5-20 ms, then fitted to the period; deadline = 1.14x measured runtime), start_time 0 ms
Peak backend utilization of the periodic set: 0.64 (budget 0.75) -- CPU 0.01/1, DSP 0.64/1, HTA 0.00/1.
Copies capped by the model bank's max_copies:
mlp_control: 2 copies -> 1 -- copies of a model are concurrent (shared period, back-to-back in the frame), and the bank allows 1 of this one at a time
Horizon 24 ms = 3.0 x hyperperiod; num_instances is ceil(horizon / period) per network, 12 operations in total.
Sporadic tasks placed in the gaps with non-overlapping windows, no edges to the periodic taskset (an edge across the boundary fans out to every periodic instance): (none).

Edges chain the copies of one model, which share its period; models at different rates get none, because workload_factory pairs periodic instances by index and that only means something at equal periods.
No p_core_speedup: it scales only the synthetic-timing fallback, so applying it on top of profiled CSVs would fabricate timings.

fused_split: FusedSensorNet cut into its two parallel conv branches plus the LSTM tail (3 tiles). This is the `fused_full` of SETUP.md's arm table -- SETUP.md's cell list for that arm is vision_conv/depth_conv/tail, which are fused_split's tiles, not the monolith's single fused_full_net cell. The split is also the only version with HTA coverage, so it is the one that exercises the third lane.

mlp_control: Control policy, 1 tile. CPU cell is the fp32 context (107.3 us): QnnCpu's int8 path returns a constant for this network regardless of input (measurements/qrb5165_v66.json, _correctness_note in bindings/mlp_control.json). HTA is capability-excluded (elu_s8), so its profile row carries the derived exclusion cost.
